text:
Peyton Krebs has 13 points in 25 games and 12 of them are assists. He has one goal, scoring on 5.9% of his shots against a league rate of 13.5%, on 3.1 expected goals. That gap closes with time. He's getting the looks, just not finishing them, and he only has 17 shots, so even a couple of goals moves the number a lot.

The rest of his game is solid. Buffalo breaks even at 5v5 with him on the ice (52.8% of shot attempts, 50% of expected goals), his minutes are up two a night over his last ten, and the Sabres have scored 9 more goals than expected with him on the ice, which explains the pile of assists. He plays like Ivan Barbashev or Marcus Johansson: a passer first, with speed.

The Athletic's Matthew Fairburn called his setup of Noah Östlund on Nov. 23 a beautiful pass. Evolving-Hockey had him 93rd among 401 forwards last season, though they also flagged that his results ran ahead of his chances. This year it's the opposite for his own shot.
headline: Krebs keeps setting up goals, and one is his
